A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BTTF research work. The main text, supplementary Sections A–E, equations, figures, and tables are readable and matchable despite rearrangement of the references and supplementary material.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-counterfactual experiments, classifier evaluations, ablations, and baseline comparisons in Section 4 and the supplement, including Tables 1, 2, and S3.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results on motion, emotion, and action classification, including quantitative comparisons, generated counterfactual examples, and the spurious-feature case study.

M1.justification: Both versions retain first-frame conditioning, latent inversion, cross-entropy plus style-loss optimization, and progressive denoising. The losses and Algorithms 1–2 are substantively unchanged. The revised inversion-iteration budget concerns experimental settings and their documentation.

E1.justification: Both use Shape-Moving for motion classification, MEAD for emotion classification, NTU RGB+D for action classification, and CelebV-Text for generator fine-tuning. No dataset, task, domain, or distinct test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: PGD Attack remains the comparator in Table 2 and Figure 7. Appendix Table S3 retains CG-Frame, CG-Video-Mid, and CG-Video with the same comparison roles. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Table S1 changes A-swinR inversion iterations from a fixed 40 to 0–40. Appendix B now specifies manual selection according to the semantic gap between original and target classes. This revises a stated experimental setting; the PDFs do not establish that results were rerun. Other reported budgets, preprocessing, splits, and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The inversion/style-loss ablations in Figure 6, spurious kicking/dodging feature analysis in Figure 8, and supplementary qualitative examples are retained. Their questions and supporting experimental evidence do not change.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed protocols, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the experimental comparisons. No statistical uncertainty reporting is added or removed.

E6.justification: Figure 3's caption corrects the reported example from an original Up video targeting Left/Down/Right to an original Down video targeting Left/Up/Right, matching the graphic already shown in v1. This is a localized result-description correction. Numerical results in Tables 1, 2, and S3 and the other reported findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The diffusion background, optimization losses, and metric formulas remain mathematically equivalent. Equation renumbering and the reordered arguments of the counterfactual loss introduce no new definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: meaningful video counterfactual editing, proximity and realism through the two-stage framework, progressive optimization, classifier faithfulness, and detection of spurious features. Local wording edits do not substantively change these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly explains why larger semantic gaps between action classes motivate fewer inversion iterations. Section 5 adds automatic hyperparameter adaptation as future work and reframes metric limitations around semantic or causal validity. Existing computational and domain-fine-tuning limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page pointer for code and results, identifies DiffSynth-Studio and MMAction2 as implementation sources, and specifies an 80GB NVIDIA A100 for the previously reported approximately two-hour generation time. It also documents the inversion-iteration selection heuristic. These are additional disclosures; linked resources were not accessed.

R1.justification: v2 replaces Halgren et al.'s molecular-docking GLIDE reference with Nichol et al.'s image-generation GLIDE work. It also consolidates duplicate references to Latent Diffusion Counterfactual Explanations while retaining that work. The broader positioning against image-based counterfactual methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose and terminology edits, rewrites the limitations section, updates affiliations, and places references before the supplementary material. The main narrative and section organization otherwise remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn into separate inversion and generation panels. Other figures receive formatting and labeling refinements, including corrected captions in Figures 3 and 8 and explicit metric labels in Figure 7. Tables S1 and S3 relocate within the supplement; the existing visual experiments and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves clarity and reproducibility through the clearer method diagram, corrected captions and GLIDE citation, implementation-source pointers, hardware disclosure, and explanation of inversion tuning. These resolve limited documentation deficiencies without expanding the empirical evidence. Per-example inversion choices and whether experiments were rerun remain unspecified, limiting the improvement.
